sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation

intro.text: NextPlat Corp (“NextPlat,” “the Company,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) is a global e-commerce and healthcare services company that operates through two reportable segments: e-Commerce Operations and Healthcare Operations. Through these segments, the Company provides satellite-enabled communication products and services, global online distribution capabilities, pharmacy services, healthcare technology solutions, and data analytics services. Our platforms serve consumers, enterprises, healthcare providers, government organizations, and other institutions across multiple geographic markets. For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 27% of revenue was generated by our e-Commerce segment and 73% by our healthcare segment.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
Stock-based compensation is accounted for based on the requirements of the Share-Based Payment Topic of ASC 718 which requires recognition in the consolidated financial statements of the cost of employee and director services received in exchange for an award of equity instruments over the period the employee or director is required to perform the services in exchange for the award (presumptively, the vesting period). The ASC also requires measurement of the cost of employee and director services received in exchange for an award based on the grant-date fair value of the award.

In June 2018, the FASB issued ASU 2018-07, Compensation – Stock Compensation. (Topic 718). This update is intended to reduce cost and complexity and to improve financial reporting for share-based payments issues to non-employees (for example, service providers, external legal counsel, suppliers, etc.). The ASU expanded the scope of ASC 718, Compensation - Stock Compensation, which previously only included share-based payments issued to employees, to also includes share-based payments issues to non-employees for goods and services. Consequently, the accounting for share-based payment to non-employees and employees will be substantially aligned. This standard became effective for the financial statements issued by public companies for the annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2018.

Our net revenues consist of e-Commerce sales of satellite phones, tracking devices, accessories, and airtime plans; pharmacy prescription revenues; and pharmacy 340B contract revenues. For the year ended December 31, 2025, overall revenues were approximately $54.3 million compared to $66.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, a decrease of approximately $11.8 million or 17.8%.

Total e-Commerce revenues were approximately $14.6 million and $13.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, an increase of approximately $0.8 million primarily due to an increase in airtime and hardware sales of approximately $0.4 million and a favorable foreign currency impact of approximately $0.4 million.

Total pharmacy prescription and other revenue, net of PBM fees, were approximately $35.7 million and $41.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, a decrease of approximately $6.2 million. The decrease was attributable to the decrease in the number of total prescriptions filled of approximately $11.3 million, which was offset by the increase in reimbursement rates per prescription filled of approximately $5.1 million. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we filled approximately 374,000 prescriptions versus 473,000 in the prior year period.

Pharmacy Prescription and Other Revenue,.text: Total pharmacy prescription and other revenue, net of PBM fees, were approximately $35.7 million and $41.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, a decrease of approximately $6.2 million. The decrease was attributable to the decrease in the number of total prescriptions filled of approximately $11.3 million, which was offset by the increase in reimbursement rates per prescription filled of approximately $5.1 million. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we filled approximately 374,000 prescriptions versus 473,000 in the prior year period. The decline in prescription volume during the current year period was influenced in part by the continued changes in provider relationships and shifts in patient flow due to insurance network adjustments or provider decisions to align with different pharmacy partners.

E-Commerce Revenue.text: Total e-Commerce revenues were approximately $14.6 million and $13.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, an increase of approximately $0.8 million primarily due to an increase in airtime and hardware sales of approximately $0.4 million and a favorable foreign currency impact of approximately $0.4 million.

Pharmacy 340B Contract.text: Our net revenues consist of e-Commerce sales of satellite phones, tracking devices, accessories, and airtime plans; pharmacy prescription revenues; and pharmacy 340B contract revenues. For the year ended December 31, 2025, overall revenues were approximately $54.3 million compared to $66.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, a decrease of approximately $11.8 million or 17.8%.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 27% of revenue was generated by our e-Commerce segment and 73% by our healthcare segment.
A significant portion of our revenue is generated through third-party marketplaces, particularly Amazon, which represented approximately 31% of total e-Commerce revenue in 2025.

Our Amazon online marketplaces represented approximately 31% and 33% of e-Commerce revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively, and we anticipate that these marketplaces will continue to represent a significant portion of our revenue for the foreseeable future.
Amazon marketplaces represented approximately 31% and 33% of our total e-Commerce revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, our revenue in China represented less than 1% of our consolidated revenues and did not have a material impact on our results of operations.
Amazon accounted for 31.1 % and 32.8 % of the Company’s net revenues during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , respectively.
No other customer accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s net revenues for either period.

Our e-Commerce operations generate revenue from two primary sources: (i) product sales including satellite phones, tracking devices, broadband terminals, and related equipment and (ii) recurring service revenue including satellite airtime subscriptions, messaging plans, and connectivity services.
Our MSS products rely on satellite networks for voice, data and tracking connectivity and thus are not reliant on cell towers or other local infrastructure.

Government organizations, including military and intelligence agencies and disaster response agencies, non-governmental organizations and industrial operations and support teams depend on mobile voice and data satellite communications products and services on a regular basis.
This diversification reasonably permits the Company not to rely on any single customer, or group of customers, on any single product line, or any specific geographic area.

Our ability to recruit qualified personnel, attract new institutional and retail clients, and expand the reach of our pharmacy operations relies on our ability to quickly adapt to changing societal attitudes, market pressure, and government regulation.
We have maintained a relationship with a primary supplier that accounted for 98% of pharmaceutical purchases for the year ended December 31, 2025, and several supplementary suppliers.
Our primary supplier for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was McKesson.

Our ability to achieve profitability depends on numerous factors, many of which are outside of our control, including growth in revenue, management of operating expenses, the stability of supply chains, reimbursement levels within our healthcare segment, competitive pressures, and overall economic conditions.
Approximately 98% of our pharmaceutical purchases for the year ended December 31, 2025 were obtained from a single wholesale distributor.
We also rely on Amazon’s fulfillment services to provide expedited shipping.
Our e-Commerce operations depend on global suppliers, manufacturers and logistics providers.
We rely on third-party manufacturers and suppliers for satellite phones, tracking devices, broadband terminals and other products.
The timing, as well as the number and value of shares repurchased under the program, will depend on a variety of factors.
The purchases from this significant vendor were approximately 98.0 % of total vendor purchases for the year ended December 31, 2025 .
